questions.answer: Belief about capability to perform actions in context.

questions.prompt: Can nervousness coexist with competent communication?
What should a communication rubric avoid?
questions.answer: Irrelevant style requirements and personal character judgments.

questions.prompt: What if the learner lacks instructions?
questions.answer: Address the access or instruction barrier first.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only; use answer-specific feedback.
scoring.practice: Separates perceived capability, observed skill and contextual barriers and selects task-appropriate support.
scoring.transfer: Create a fictional confidence-skill matrix for a social task, with four scenarios and differentiated support options. Define two observable criteria and one accessibility alternative. Explain what the matrix cannot establish about the learner.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
